messages:
incident-bot: PAGE: Serving runtime alert - model-load failures observed for model 'redwood/xl-quant-v2' across us-west-2 cluster. Error rate spike: 12% requests failing during warmup. Severity: P1.

alice (oncall): on it. seeing repeated pod restarts in gs-infer-*-pool. logs show exit code 137 on container start.

maria (eng-runtime): 137 usually OOM during load. Any stack traces?

alice (oncall): pasted first failing container log snippet:```
[2026-03-15T09:10:02Z] loader: starting deserialization of weights
[2026-03-15T09:10:04Z] loader: allocate tensor buffers 37.4GB
[2026-03-15T09:10:04Z] runtime: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[2026-03-15T09:10:04Z] loader: fatal: failed to map weights: Unexpected EOF
Exit status 137
```

maria (eng-runtime): that matches OOM at load. This model's quantized checkpoint is larger than expected on these nodes. Could be a regression in quantization tooling or kernel selection.

bob (sre): also seeing node flaps: kubelet evicting pods due to memory pressure on g-w1-usw2-03. Node memory usage at 98%. Events: `OOMKilled` for multiple pods.

jamal (eng-platform): checking autoscaler logs. There was a scheduled batch job yesterday that consumed GPU memory but shouldn't block node-level RAM. Might be loose memory limits on the model init container.

alice (oncall): initial mitigation: pausing rollouts for redwood/xl-quant-v2 and moving new traffic to redwood/xl-quant-v1 fallback. Executing routing change now. @maria please verify compatibility for reroute.

maria (eng-runtime): confirmed v1 is ABI-compatible for inference API. Triggering weighted routing to move 80% -> v1, 20% -> v2 for canary.

sophia (product): status for customers? Which tenants hit errors?

kevin (cs): Customer telemetry: two enterprise customers (acme-corp, lumenai) reported degraded responses. Estimated 4% of overall customer traffic affected pre-mitigation. I'll message ACME rep with the known cause (model warmup OOM) and mitigation actions.

alice (oncall): rolling restart planned but hold until nodes stabilized. For now cordon g-w1-usw2-03 and drain non-critical pods to free memory. @bob you have node-level ops?

bob (sre): cordoning node and moving stateless infra now. Running `kubectl cordon g-w1-usw2-03` then `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data`. Will monitor memory reclaim.

maria (eng-runtime): while node stabilizes, short-term workaround: reduce model load concurrency to 1 per GPU for v2 via runtime config. That should prevent simultaneous weight allocations. Applying config:```yaml
model_load:
  max_concurrent_loads: 1
  load_timeout_s: 120
```
Applying now.

alice (oncall): applied. Also lowered kube pod memory request for model init phase (experimental): added init container memory limit 8Gi to force OOM earlier? wait we want more memory — revert that.

maria (eng-runtime): good catch — we should *increase* memory for init container. I'll patch deployment to ensure init container has 48Gi request on nodes with large GPUs. Pushing hotfix.

jamal (eng-platform): FYI there's a failing path in our deserializer that surfaces `Unexpected EOF` when model checkpoint metadata mismatches expected size. Could be corrupt checkpoint too. Checking artifact storage checksum for the latest upload.

maria (eng-runtime): if checkpoint is corrupt, loads will consistently fail across nodes. Are failures happening on the same artifact version?

alice (oncall): logs show model_version: 2026-03-14-2130 for failing loads. Some nodes loaded it earlier today successfully but later attempts fail — hints at nondeterministic memory pressure + partial writes?

jamal (eng-platform): artifact storage reports object size 42,987,312,102 bytes, checksum mismatch on one replica during fetch `err=ShortRead`. Re-fetching clean copy from primary archive.

kevin (cs): communicated to ACME: "We identified warmup OOMs during model load for the new quantized checkpoint. We're rerouting traffic to a stable model variant and performing node restarts. We'll follow up with root cause."

alice (oncall): quick customer impact summary for incident log: ~4% of production requests saw 5xx during warmup windows, primarily affecting long-running associates. No data leakage.

bob (sre): node memory reclaimed after draining; memory back to 60%. Restarted runtime pool pods sequentially to avoid thundering herd. Observed one pod hit compile timeout: `triton_compile: timeout after 30s` then retried and succeeded.

maria (eng-runtime): compile timeout might be separate but related: our kernel compiler takes longer on some quantized kernels. I increased compile timeout to 120s in runtime config and bumped compiler concurrency to 2.

jamal (eng-platform): artifact reupload complete, checksum validated. Redeploying v2 from fresh artifact and keeping weighted routing diverted.

alice (oncall): redeploy started. Monitoring load logs.

maria (eng-runtime): initial warms look good: deserialization completes, no cudaMalloc failures. Running small scale canary to verify long-tail.

kevin (cs): ACME updated: "Thanks for the fast mitigation and the re-route. We'll wait for your signal before reverting traffic."

alice (oncall): after 25m of stable canary, shifting traffic back to v2 at 10% increments.

sophia (product): please include potential customer-facing language for postmortem: cause = artifact checksum mismatch + node memory pressure leading to OOM at load for quantized checkpoint; mitigation = reroute to stable model, node drain, artifact reupload, runtime config fixes; next steps = add artifact validation + safer load concurrency defaults.

maria (eng-runtime): filing follow-ups: 1) add artifact checksum verification during upload (platform), 2) default max_concurrent_loads=1 for quantized models, 3) monitor compile durations and fail fast for stuck compiles.

bob (sre): follow-ups: automate cordon-and-drain runbook for memory pressure, add ephemeral eviction alerts.

jamal (eng-platform): I'll open infra ticket to surface artifact replication errors earlier and add parity checks.

alice (oncall): incident status: mitigated -> degraded-> recover. Moving to monitoring phase. Logging incident start/end times to tracker.

incident-bot: Incident 2026-03-15T09:10:01Z -> 2026-03-15T09:27:15Z: Mitigated. Postmortem P1 required. Assigned: maria (eng-runtime), jamal (eng-platform), bob (sre).

kevin (cs): will send postmortem notice to impacted customers once draft ready.

sophia (product): thanks team. I'll schedule a cross-functional review tomorrow.

alice (oncall): handing off to night oncall @ben at 09:30 UTC. Ben please watch for any re-occurrence.

ben (oncall): ack, watching.
